answer: One cipher per sealed host: a cipher registers in bridge only against a distinct hardware-sealed key, so clones of one machine collide at the same anchor and the later ones are refused. Enrolling the kth host burns umber equal to the hosts already sealed in bridge, read at commit and not reservable, so a thousand cipher cost a thousand machines plus 500,500 umber, the bill attached to each host enrolment. It breaks if host keys can be virtualised or resold.
